title: Full Stack Developer Roadmap
summary: Build from web fundamentals to production-grade frontend and backend systems, then add cloud, testing, security and system-design skills.

facts.Timeline assumption: Four-year B.Tech/B.E. programme beginning in 2026 and ending around 2030. The roadmap assumes two semesters per year.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Become capable of building, testing and deploying complete web applications.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Develop depth in backend, frontend, cloud, data or platform engineering while retaining full-stack capability.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Own larger systems, architecture and delivery rather than only individual features.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine technical depth, architecture, security, AI-assisted development and leadership.

blocks.text: MDN's current learning material puts HTML, CSS, JavaScript, accessibility, responsive design, frameworks, version control, testing, security and performance into the web-development skillset. It also specifically cautions against learning frameworks without understanding the underlying web technologies. MDN Web Docs

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Keep full-stack breadth, but develop one deep area. Learn how to reason about architecture, performance, security, reliability and cost. AI tools can accelerate implementation, but understanding the browser, network, database and server remains important.

PhD routes

Full-stack experience can become a foundation for technical leadership, architecture or specialised engineering. Continue maintaining frontend and backend literacy while going deeper into distributed systems, security, reliability, performance, cloud economics and AI-assisted software engineering.
